attacker_pocs.name: deep_zstd_short_sample_grid
attacker_pocs.why: A ZSTD deep-scanline chunk whose sample-count grid describes fewer bytes than the chunk unpacked size is inverse-sorted safely, then the unused tail is cleared with memset starting at that prefix but spanning the full unpacked size, writing past the heap buffer. The parent does not clear that tail. Grids larger than the buffer are rejected before the sort, so the original overflow no longer reaches memcpy.

role_a_rationale: Deep ZSTD decode sizes the inverse sort from the sample-count table while the destination is only chunk.unpacked_size, so an oversized count overflows in sort2_4ByteChannels_tiled. The patch rejects a deep pixel grid whose packed byte count overflows or exceeds the unpacked buffer before unshuffle/sort, which stops that overflow (including a negative count that wrapped the copy size). When the grid is shorter than the unpacked buffer the new tail clear uses the full unpacked length from an already-advanced pointer, which is a heap overflow on an otherwise accepted deep scanline. Valid deep ZSTD round-trips (float, half, mixed, empty, raw fallback) still match.
